figures.alt: Galvanized step-flashing pieces staged course by course beside a red-brick chimney and shingle roof
figures.caption: Step flashing is a layered roof-to-masonry transition, not a single sheet of metal. The sequence needs to work with the shingle courses before the chimney counterflashing finishes the system.
figures.before: When You Need a Permit in Jacksonville

figures.alt: Roof drip edge integrated with underlayment at a Florida shingle eave
figures.caption: Roof details shed water by overlap and order. Use the same layered thinking at a chimney rather than depending on surface sealant to make up for a broken transition.

figures.alt: Finished layered flashing integrated with shingles around a curb-mounted skylight
figures.caption: A watertight roof transition only works when the surrounding roof layers are sound. If shingles, decking, or masonry are deteriorated, the chimney scope may be larger than flashing alone.
